direction.name: The Reliability Record

positioning.category: Track record platform for student teams
positioning.statement: Students build a visible record of the projects they finished, and start each new one by agreeing who carries what.
positioning.differentiator: Evidence of past follow-through plus an explicit agreement at the start of every project.
positioning.value_proposition: Pick teammates on evidence, then make the split explicit before the work begins.

direction.audience_focus: Students who have been let down by a teammate and want that not to happen again
direction.tagline_direction: Proof and fairness: what you finished, and what you owe this team
strengths: Useful in the very first project, before any record exists
The record and the agreements reinforce each other over time
risks: Two ideas in one can blur the pitch
The agreement step adds friction at the moment a team is most excited
direction.why_this_lens: The record is the wedge; the agreement is what makes it useful on day one.

outputs.merge_note: Kept the evidence-based record from A as the core claim and took the start-of-project agreement from C to solve A's cold-start problem. Dropped C's framing as an admin layer.
